answer: Reward-capped bonds resist sybils: each identity must post collateral B set to exceed the maximum reward R any single account can extract before an audit catches it, so B>=R makes every fake a guaranteed net loss once slashed. A nebula of thousands of accounts costs N*B to stand up but can drain at most N*R < N*B, so the harvest never clears the deposit. The meadow of free nectar closes: with the bond sized above extractable value, scaling the swarm only scales the loss, while honest agents recover their bond by never cheating.
